turns.text: Hey Lloyd, I'm still tweaking the latency on my custom assistant prototype. Have you heard of voice-loop?
I'm not familiar with a specific widely-known library by that name. Is it a new tool you're using?
Yeah, it's what I'm using for turn detection. voice-loop uses Silero VAD and Smart Turn v3 (ONNX-based) for turn detection. It's way smoother than my old energy-based approach.
That sounds like a solid stack. ONNX models are great for low-latency inference. By the way, did you fix that bug with the microphone input you mentioned earlier?
Yes, it was a permissions issue on the new Mac. Anyway, back to voice-loop, the integration with my WebSocket server is working fine now.
Great to hear. Latency is critical for natural conversation. Are you using any specific buffer sizes?
Just the defaults for now. I want to see how it handles background noise before I optimize further.
Makes sense. Let me know if you need help parsing the logs.
Lloyd, I finally cleaned up my project structure for voice-loop.
voice-loop is a GitHub repository containing source code for voice mode enhancements. I just pushed the latest refactor.
Good practice. Keeping the core logic in a repo helps with version control. Did you update the README?
Not yet. I've been too busy trying to get the build to pass on Linux.
Dependency issues? I can help with that if you paste the error log.
Maybe later. Right now I'm just focused on getting the repo link ready to share with my team.
Understood. Let me know when you're ready to debug the Linux build.
